subject.title: feat: Rate-limit fallback user-visible error notification (message-lifecycle Phase 2 extension)

question: Should this PR become the complete failover-notification implementation, or should the metadata-only approach be folded back into the canonical RFC work?
rationale: The code defect is clear, but maintainers need to choose the permanent delivery boundary and user-facing copy ownership before accepting a new failover message contract.

options.title: Complete Delivery Before Merge
options.body: Expand or replace the branch so the notice is actually routed through the established delivery boundary with approved copy and proof.

options.title: Keep As RFC Exploration
options.body: Leave this PR open only as partial design context while the canonical RFC or another implementation owns the complete fix.

options.title: Accept Metadata-Only Scope
options.body: Maintainers can intentionally land the optional field, but should avoid closing the RFC or claiming user-visible notification support until delivery exists.

recommendation.title: Complete Delivery Before Merge
recommendation.body: Expand or replace the branch so the notice is actually routed through the established delivery boundary with approved copy and proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest recent and historical signal across failover metadata, reply delivery, and current-main ownership of these paths.
